title: Sink-Free Attention Enables Prefix-Free Streaming KV Caches

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to show that gated attention allows stable streaming inference without preserving prefix sink tokens in the KV cache. None of the prior papers explicitly establish this empirical relationship. While papers like [8] and [17] discuss attention sinks and gated attention mechanisms, they do not demonstrate the specific effect of gated attention enabling stable streaming inference under the described KV cache regime. Similarly, [21] explores attention sinks but does not address gated attention or streaming inference stability. No prior paper reports or establishes the same empirical relationship.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves comparing vanilla and gated Qwen2-1B models under pure rolling-window (0+W) versus prefix-sink (S+(W-S)) cache regimes with cache-relative positional encoding. Paper [17] discusses gated attention mechanisms and systematically investigates their effects, including sparsity and attention-sink-free properties, which align with the gated attention primitive used here. Paper [8] explores window attention and prefix-sink caching but does not involve gated attention. Paper [30] discusses positional encoding enhancements but does not address gated attention or the specific cache regimes described. Thus, [17] covers the mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design measures the PPL ratio between pure rolling-window and prefix-sink regimes for gated versus vanilla attention. Papers like [8], [17], and [21] use similar evaluation designs involving attention mechanisms and their effects on inference performance metrics (e.g., PPL). Specifically, [17] conducts comprehensive experiments comparing gated attention variants, which aligns with the evaluation design here. While the specific models and cache regimes differ, the evaluation design itself is covered by [17].

### Domain
The domain is streaming LLM inference and KV cache management. Papers [1], [4], [8], [17], and others extensively address streaming LLM inference and KV cache optimization. For example, [8] focuses on streaming applications and KV cache challenges, while [4] surveys KV cache optimization techniques for LLM serving. These papers operate in the same general application area, even if the specific sub-problem or instance differs. Thus, the domain is covered.

### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to establish the causal mechanism linking gating to streaming stability via attention sink elimination. Paper [3] discusses the effects of gating mechanisms in attention, including their ability to eliminate attention sinks, but it does not explicitly establish a causal mechanism linking gating to streaming stability. Paper [6] identifies attention sinks as a universal phenomenon in language models and discusses their implications for streaming and other applications, but it does not establish a causal mechanism linking gating to streaming stability. Paper [10] proposes Value-State Gated Attention to mitigate attention sinks and improve model performance, but it does not explicitly establish the causal mechanism between gating and streaming stability. None of the prior papers explicitly establish the causal mechanism as described in the contribution.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves measuring the attention sink rate under post-SDPA gating and correlating low sink rates with stable streaming across all tested models. Paper [3] systematically investigates gating-augmented attention variants and their effects, including attention sink elimination, but it does not explicitly measure attention sink rates or correlate them with streaming stability. Paper [6] empirically analyzes attention sinks in language models but does not involve post-SDPA gating or correlate sink rates with streaming stability. Paper [10] addresses attention sinks using Value-State Gated Attention but does not measure sink rates or establish a correlation with streaming stability. None of the prior papers implement the exact mechanism described in the contribution.

### Evaluation
The evaluation demonstrates that gating reduces attention sink rates by 99.3-100% and that low sink rates perfectly predict stable streaming across all tested models. Paper [3] conducts comprehensive experiments on gating-augmented attention variants, but it does not evaluate the reduction in attention sink rates or their correlation with streaming stability. Paper [6] empirically analyzes attention sinks but does not evaluate the impact of gating on sink rates or streaming stability. Paper [10] evaluates Value-State Gated Attention but does not measure sink rate reduction or its predictive power for streaming stability. None of the prior papers use the same evaluation design.

### Domain
The domain is attention sink analysis in transformers. Paper [1] discusses attention sinks in large language models and their mitigation through sink-aware training. Paper [3] investigates gating mechanisms in attention, including their effects on attention sinks. Paper [6] focuses on attention sinks in language models and their implications for various applications, including streaming. Paper [10] addresses attention sinks in transformers using Value-State Gated Attention. These papers collectively cover the domain of attention sink analysis in transformers.
